newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg, Danisco, power Danish index upward.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg, Danisco, power Danish index upward.

text.p: Rallies by Carlsberg and Danisco helped push average Danish share prices up on Monday but dealers expected movement to die down ahead of a meeting of the U.S. FOMC on Tuesday and Wednesday and jobless data on Thursday.
The KFX top-20 index rose 0.89 point to 171.71 in bourse turnover of 2.19 billion crowns. Its August future rose 0.60, to 172.00 crowns, with 172 contracts of 100,000 crowns traded.

Carlsberg closed 10.00 crowns up at 366.00 crowns, recouping losses suffered on Friday after the British government blocked the planned sale of its half of joint venture Carlsberg-Tetley to partner Bass.
Danisco made four crowns, to close at 406.00. It took a fall last week when it announced a 14 percent rise in 1996/97 profits but said the rate of growth would be less in 1997/98.
Sophus Berendsen fell 15.00 crowns to 960.00, tracking declines by British services group Rentokil Initial in which it holds a 35.8 percent holding. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
